title: Easy Read summaries
rule: Easy Read uses short sentences, one idea in each, everyday words and a picture beside every sentence. Each summary says what the screen is for and the first thing you can do there. It does not replace the screen: it helps you decide whether to read on.

home: Amplify helps young people be heard.
It is for young people and the adults who help them.
Pick a part of the portal from the menu on the left.
corner: This page is about fair ways to listen to young people.
Everyone should get a chance to take part.
It explains four big ideas, one at a time.
route: This page shows the steps to having a say.
The steps go from a school council up to Parliament.
Use the map to find what happens where you live.
state: This page explains who runs the country.
There is Parliament, there are governments and there are councils.
It shows where young people can be heard.
numbers: This page shows facts about young people in the UK.
It covers who they are and how they live.
Each chart says in plain words what it means.
issues: This page shows 16 things young people campaign about.
The charts show which topics young people voted for most.
Pick a topic to see who decides it.
guide: This page has tours of the portal.
A tour shows you around, step by step.
Pick the tour that fits you.
hub: This page tells the story of one petition.
It shows how many people signed it.
It shows what happened after it closed.
momentum: It works out how fast a campaign would need to grow.
It is a guess for planning, not a promise.
plan: This page helps you pick a good time to start a campaign.
It shows exam times and school holidays.
Tick the list to check you are ready.
coal: This page is about finding people to help.
Groups and adults can back your campaign.
It shows who might help and how.
kit: This page has ready-made messages and posters.
You can change them to fit your campaign.
Check the words before you use them.
pledge: This page shows how a pledge wall could work.
The pledges here are examples, not real people.
A pledge you make stays on this device.
radar: This page lists news and dates to watch.
Some dates are good moments to speak up.
Each item says where the news came from.
policy: This page shows government plans for young people.
It shows how much money each plan has.
Ask for things the government already promised.
map: This page has a map of the UK's areas for MPs.
Find your area on the map.
acad: Each lesson ends with one question.
Your progress stays on this device.
ysc: This page is about the Youth Select Committee.
Young people ask questions of people in charge.
It shows what the committee looked into.
post: This page looks at past campaigns.
Learning from it helps the next campaign.
track: Things changed because young people spoke up.
Each change says where the facts came from.
prof: This page is about Members of Youth Parliament.
They come from every part of the UK.
The profile shown is an example, not a real person.
incl: This page is about reaching every young person.
Some young people are heard less than others.
It lists what the portal does to include everyone.
res: This page has things to use where you are.
There are packs for schools, clubs and homes.
Pick your setting to see your pack.
ai: This page is about computer helpers called AI.
It shows ideas, not things that work yet.
AI can make mistakes, so always check.
brand: This page shows the portal's colours and shapes.
Designers use it to make things look the same.
You can skip it if you are not designing.
care: This page is about staying safe.
It says who to talk to if you are worried.
graph: It shows how ideas link to each other.
Search for a word to find its meaning.
sources: This page lists websites you can trust.
You can sort them by topic and by nation.
Each one says when it was last checked.
latest: This page has the latest news for young people.
Each item says where it came from.
changes: This page lists changes to the portal.
Newest changes are at the top.
Each change has a number and a date.
trust: This page is about keeping people safe.
It has rules for different ages.
It covers sign languages and every voice.
health: This page checks the portal is working.
It shows what is out of date.
It shows problems still being fixed.
about: This page says who made Amplify and why.
It says what Amplify wants to achieve.
It is a project for young people.
launch: This page is about launching Amplify.
The launch is in UK Parliament Week, 23 to 27 November 2026.
It has links you can share.
communities: This page lists groups where young people meet.
There are youth councils, parliaments and clubs.
media: This page is for people writing about Amplify.
It has pictures you are allowed to use.
help: This page helps you use the portal.
It has a manual and short guides.
feedback: This page is for telling us what you think.
You use a form, not email.
involve: This page is about helping to build the portal.
There are jobs for a few minutes or longer.
Pick a job that fits you.
ambassadors: This page is about helping to spread the word.
There are three roles to choose from.
Signing up is paused for now, to keep people safe.
campaign: This page has posters and posts to share.
There is a short script for a school assembly.
It has dates to plan around.
learn: This page has lesson plans for group leaders.
Each plan says how long it takes.
stem: This page is about science and technology.
It shows free courses and jobs.
Girls and young women are welcome in tech.
research: This page is about asking users what works.
Designers can help improve the portal.
Signing up is paused for now, to keep people safe.
service: This page describes the people the portal is for.
It shows the steps each person takes.
It shows what happens behind each screen.
golive: This page lists what must be ready before going public.
It shows what has been tested.
It shows what is still to do.
product: This page says where Amplify is going.
It lists what is planned next.
Each plan links to the work behind it.
notify: This page lets you choose your alerts.
You can bring back alerts you closed.
parliament: This page shows how Parliament works.
It shows a normal day and week there.
It shows what different people in Parliament do.
civic: This page shows every way to take part.
It shows what you can do at each age.
Some rules are different in each nation.
